questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I went to a fairly ordinary state school on the edge of town, but I have a real soft spot for it. questions.uzSampleA2:
Mening maktabim yaxshi.

U katta va unda ko'p o'quvchilar bor.

Men u yerda futbol o'ynashni yaxshi ko'raman va do'stlarimni yaxshi ko'raman.

Lekin uyga vazifalarni yoqtirmayman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Mening maktabim juda yaxshi joy. Menimcha, u ancha katta, ko'p sinf xonalari va katta o'yingoh maydoniga ega.

O'qituvchilar odatda yaxshi va yordam berishga tayyor, va menga ba'zi fanlarim, masalan tarix va san'at yoqadi.

Lekin, matematika menga unchalik yoqmaydi.

Mening fikrimcha, maktabimning eng yaxshi tomoni bu do'stlarim.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Mening maktabim shahar chekkasida joylashgan o'rta maktab. U nisbatan zamonaviy bino, yaxshi jihozlarga ega, garchi ba'zi joylarni yangilash kerak bo'lsa ham.

O'qitish sifati asosan yaxshi va ba'zi o'qituvchilarning darslarni qiziqarli qilish uchun qilayotgan harakatlarini qadrlayman.

Maktabda darsdan tashqari mashg'ulotlarning keng doirasi mavjud, bu juda yaxshi, chunki u o'quvchilarga sinfdan tashqari qiziqishlarini o'rganishga imkon beradi.

Garchi eng gavjum paytlarda haddan tashqari ko'p odam bo'lish muammolari bo'lsa-da, umuman olganda, u mustahkam ta'lim asosini ta'minlaydi deb o'ylayman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Tell me about your school.
idioms: school days are the best days - "maktab kunlari eng yaxshi kunlar"
pass with flying colors - "a'lo baho bilan o'tmoq"
sentenceStarters: "I attended a school called..." - "Men ... nomli maktabda o'qidim..."
"What I particularly enjoyed about my school was..." - "Maktabimda ayniqsa yoqtirgan narsa..."
"Looking back, I would say that my school..." - "Orqaga qarasam, maktabim ... derdim..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I attended a public secondary school in my hometown, which I graduated from a few years ago. It was a fairly large school with about 1,500 students and a dedicated teaching staff.
The school had excellent facilities including a well-equipped library, computer labs, and sports grounds. I particularly enjoyed the science labs where we conducted hands-on experiments.
What I loved most about my school was the supportive atmosphere. The teachers were genuinely invested in our success and always encouraged us to pursue our interests. I made lifelong friends there and have many fond memories. As they say, "School days are the best days of your life," and I definitely agree with that sentiment.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men o'z shahrimdagi davlat o'rta maktabida o'qiganman va uni bir necha yil oldin tugatganman. U taxminan 1500 nafar o'quvchi va fidoyi o'qituvchilar jamoasiga ega bo'lgan ancha katta maktab edi.

Maktabda yaxshi jihozlangan kutubxona, kompyuter laboratoriyalari va sport maydonchalari kabi ajoyib imkoniyatlar mavjud edi. Men ayniqsa, amaliy tajribalar o'tkazganimiz fan laboratoriyalaridan zavqlanardim.

Maktabimda menga eng yoqqan narsa - bu qo'llab-quvvatlovchi muhit edi. O'qituvchilar bizning muvaffaqiyatimizga chin dildan qiziqishardi va bizni doimo o'z qiziqishlarimizni davom ettirishga undashardi. U yerda umrbod do'stlar orttirdim va ko'plab yaxshi xotiralarim bor. Aytishlaricha, "Maktab yillari hayotingizning eng yaxshi kunlari", va men bu fikrga albatta qo'shilaman.

Men yozni yaxshi ko'raman.

Men suzaman.

Men haroratning o'zgarishini juda qadrlayman; juda issiq ham emas, juda sovuq ham emas, tashqarida bo'lish uchun aynan mos.

Kuz bilan bog'liq ma'lum bir qulaylik hissi ham bor, xuddi iliq ichimlik va yaxshi kitob bilan uyda qolishni xohlagandek. Bu yilning juda yoqimli vaqti.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - What is your favorite season?
idioms: "Every cloud has a silver lining" - "Har bir bulutning kumush qirrasi bor"
save for a rainy day - "qora kun uchun saqlamoq"
sentenceStarters: "My favorite season is definitely..." - "Mening sevimli faslim, albatta..."
"What I particularly love about this season is..." - "Bu faslda ayniqsa yoqtirgan narsa..."
"I find that during this season, I feel..." - "Bu faslda men ... his qilaman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
My absolute favorite season is autumn. I genuinely love everything about it – the changing colors of the leaves, the crisp air, and the comfortable temperatures.
What I particularly appreciate about autumn is the beautiful scenery. Watching the leaves turn from green to vibrant shades of orange, red, and gold is truly breathtaking. It feels like nature is putting on a spectacular show.
I also enjoy the cozy atmosphere that autumn brings. It's the perfect time for warm drinks, comfortable sweaters, and walks in the park. The weather is neither too hot nor too cold – just perfectly pleasant. As poets often say, autumn is a season that touches the soul with its melancholic beauty.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening eng sevimli faslim kuz. Men uning hamma narsasini chin dildan yaxshi ko'raman – barglarning o'zgaruvchan ranglari, tiniq havo va qulay harorat.

Kuzning ayniqsa qadrlaydigan jihati – bu go'zal manzarasi. Barglarning yashildan to'q sariq, qizil va oltin ranglarga o'zgarishini tomosha qilish chindan ham hayratlanarli. Go'yo tabiat ajoyib tomosha ko'rsatayotgandek tuyuladi.

Men kuz olib keladigan shinam muhitdan ham zavqlanaman. Bu issiq ichimliklar, qulay sviterlar va parkda sayr qilish uchun eng zo'r vaqt. Ob-havo na juda issiq, na juda sovuq – shunchaki mukammal darajada yoqimli. Shoirlar ko'pincha aytganidek, kuz – o'zining xomush go'zalligi bilan ruhga ta'sir qiladigan fasl.

questions.prompt: What do you usually do on weekends?
questions.sampleA1: I like weekends. I play games. I eat food. I sleep.
questions.sampleA2: On weekends, I usually relax at home. I watch TV and play video games. Sometimes I go to the park with my family. I like weekends because I don't go to school.
questions.sampleB1: Well, on weekends I usually try to relax. I often sleep in late because I'm tired from the week. Then, I might hang out with my friends, maybe go to the cinema or a cafe. I also need to do some chores, like cleaning my room. I think weekends are important for recharging.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the thing is, my weekends are usually a bit of a mix. On Saturdays I tend to have a lie-in and then catch up with friends over coffee. Sundays are a bit quieter — I'll get on top of my chores and maybe unwind with a good film. To be honest, I just need to recharge my batteries before the week kicks off again.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men dam olish kunlarini yaxshi ko'raman. Men o'yinlar o'ynayman. Men ovqat yeyman. Men uxlayman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Dam olish kunlari men odatda uyda dam olaman. Men televizor ko'raman va video o'yinlar o'ynayman. Ba'zida oilam bilan parkga boraman. Dam olish kunlarini yaxshi ko'raman, chunki maktabga bormayman.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, dam olish kunlari men odatda dam olishga harakat qilaman. Ko'pincha kechgacha uxlayman, chunki hafta davomida charchagan bo'laman. Keyin, do'stlarim bilan vaqt o'tkazishim mumkin, balki kinoga yoki kafega borarmiz. Shuningdek, xonamni tozalash kabi ba'zi uy ishlarini ham qilishim kerak. Menimcha, dam olish kunlari kuch yig'ish uchun muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Dam olish kunlari odatda dam olish va hafta davomida vaqtim bo'lmagan ishlarni bajarish aralashmasidan iborat. Men albatta dam olishga vaqt ajratishga harakat qilaman, balki kitob o'qish yoki film tomosha qilish orqali. Shuningdek, do'stlar bilan tushlik qilish yoki mahalliy tadbirga borish orqali muloqot qilishga harakat qilaman. Albatta, har doim bajarilishi kerak bo'lgan ishlar va uy vazifalari bor, lekin men ularni yanada yoqimli mashg'ulotlar bilan muvozanatlashga harakat qilaman. Gap shundaki, bu menga tetik va kelgusi haftaga tayyor bo'lishimga imkon beradigan ritmni topishdan iborat.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - What do you usually do on weekends?
idioms: "All work and no play" - "Faqat ish va dam olish yo'q"
sentenceStarters: "On weekends, I typically enjoy..." - "Dam olish kunlari men odatda ... dan zavqlanaman..."
"I usually spend my Saturdays..." - "Men odatda shanba kunlarimni ... o'tkazaman..."
"Sundays are usually reserved for..." - "Yakshanba kunlari odatda ... uchun ajratilgan..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
On weekends, I typically like to balance relaxation with productive activities. After a busy week, I need some time to recharge my batteries.
Saturday mornings are usually spent sleeping in and enjoying a leisurely breakfast. In the afternoon, I often meet up with friends for coffee or lunch. We might catch up on each other's lives or watch a movie together.
Sundays are a bit more structured. I try to do some household chores, prepare meals for the week ahead, and perhaps do some studying or personal projects. I also enjoy outdoor activities like jogging or cycling when the weather permits. Essentially, weekends are my time to wind down and prepare for the coming week.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Dam olish kunlarida men odatda dam olishni samarali mashg'ulotlar bilan muvozanatlashni yoqtiraman. Band haftadan so'ng, men biroz vaqt davomida kuch yig'ishim kerak.

Shanba kunlari ertalab odatda uzoqroq uxlash va bemalol nonushta qilish bilan o'tadi. Tushdan keyin men ko'pincha do'stlarim bilan qahva ichish yoki tushlik qilish uchun uchrashaman. Biz bir-birimizning hayotimizdan xabar olishimiz yoki birgalikda kino tomosha qilishimiz mumkin.

Yakshanba kunlari biroz ko'proq rejalashtirilgan bo'ladi. Men uy ishlarining bir qismini bajarishga, kelgusi hafta uchun ovqat tayyorlashga va ehtimol, biroz o'qish yoki shaxsiy loyihalar bilan shug'ullanishga harakat qilaman. Ob-havo imkon bersa, yugurish yoki velosipedda sayr qilish kabi ochiq havoda mashg'ulotlardan ham zavqlanaman. Aslida, dam olish kunlari - bu mening dam olishim va kelgusi haftaga tayyorgarlik ko'rishim uchun vaqtdir.

questions.sampleB1:
In the pictures, I see two ways to travel. First, there is a family going on an airplane.

They look happy. The second picture shows a woman on a train.

She is looking out the window at the scenery. I think train travel is relaxing.

Air travel is faster, however.
questions.sampleB2: These two pictures show two different ways of travelling. In the first one, there's a family walking across the tarmac towards a plane — the mum and dad are swinging their little girl up between them, and they're wheeling along a blue and a yellow suitcase. They look over the moon. The second picture shows a woman leaning out of a train window, taking in the view as it winds through lush tea plantations. To be honest, it sums up the contrast nicely — flying is all about speed, whereas the train is more about soaking up the scenery.

questions.uzSampleB1:
Rasmlarda men sayohat qilishning ikki xil usulini ko'ryapman. Birinchidan, samolyotda ketayotgan oila bor.

Ular baxtli ko'rinadi. Ikkinchi rasmda poyezdda ketayotgan ayol ko'rsatilgan.

U derazadan manzaraga qarab turibdi. Menimcha, poyezdda sayohat qilish dam beradi.

questions.uzSampleB2:
Rasmlarda turli xil sayohat tajribalari tasvirlangan. Birinchi rasmda bir oila samolyot tomon yurib ketayotganini ko'rish mumkin, ehtimol, ular sayohatga otlanmoqchi. Ular xursand va ta'tilga tayyor ko'rinadi.

Ikkinchi rasmda poyezdda ketayotgan va derazadan manzaradan zavqlanayotgan ayolni ko'rish mumkin. U go'zal qishloq joylaridan sayohat qilayotganga o'xshaydi.

Bu ikki transport turining o'rtasidagi farqni ko'rib chiqish qiziq. Havo transporti ko'pincha tezlik va samaradorlik haqida bo'lsa, poyezdda sayohat qilish ko'proq sayohatning o'zi haqida bo'lishi mumkin, bu esa manzaradan bahramand bo'lish va dam olish imkoniyatini beradi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
sentenceStarters: "In the first picture, I can see..." - "Birinchi rasmda men ... ko'ryapman..."
"The second image shows..." - "Ikkinchi rasm ... ko'rsatmoqda..."
"These pictures contrast two different ways of..." - "Bu rasmlar ... ning ikki xil usulini taqqoslaydi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
In these two pictures, I can see different modes of transportation that people use for traveling.
The first image shows a happy family – what appears to be parents with their young child – walking on an airport tarmac towards an airplane. They're pulling colorful suitcases, with the child carrying a bright yellow one. The family seems excited and clearly ready for their journey. They're all wearing casual clothes and face masks, suggesting this might be during or after the pandemic period. The atmosphere is one of anticipation and family adventure.
The second picture presents a completely different travel experience. We see a woman leaning out of a train window, taking photographs of the stunning scenery around her. The train is traveling through what looks like lush green tea plantations or hills. She appears to be enjoying the journey itself, capturing the beautiful natural landscape.
These images effectively contrast two ways of traveling – air travel, which is fast but less scenic, and train travel, which allows passengers to truly appreciate the landscape. Both have their own unique charm and appeal to different types of travelers.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki suratda odamlarning sayohat qilish uchun foydalanadigan turli transport turlarini ko'rishim mumkin.

Birinchi suratda baxtli oilani ko'rish mumkin – ota-onalar va ularning kichkina farzandi aeroportning uchish-qo'nish yo'lagida samolyot tomon yurishmoqda. Ular rang-barang chamadonlarni sudrab ketishyapti, bola esa yorqin sariq chamadonni ko'tarib olgan. Oilaning kayfiyati a'lo va ular aniq sayohatga tayyor. Ularning barchasi kundalik kiyimda va niqobda, bu esa pandemiya davrida yoki undan keyingi davr bo'lishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi. Atmosfera umid va oilaviy sarguzashtlardan iborat.

Ikkinchi surat butunlay boshqacha sayohat tajribasini taqdim etadi. Biz bir ayolni poyezd oynasidan tashqariga egilib, atrofidagi ajoyib manzaralarni suratga olayotganini ko'ramiz. Poyezd yam-yashil choy plantatsiyalari yoki tepaliklar kabi joylardan o'tmoqda. Uning o'zi sayohatdan zavqlanayotganga o'xshaydi, go'zal tabiiy landshaftni suratga olmoqda.

Bu suratlar sayohatning ikki usulini samarali ravishda solishtiradi – havo transporti, bu tez, lekin kamroq manzarali va poyezdda sayohat, bu yo'lovchilarga landshaftni chinakam qadrlash imkonini beradi. Ularning ikkalasi ham o'ziga xos jozibaga ega va turli xil sayohatchilarga yoqadi.

questions.prompt: What are some challenges people face while traveling by plane?
questions.sampleA2:
I go to airport.

It is busy and I wait.

The plane is late, and I am sad.

My bag is heavy, and I don't like it.
questions.sampleB1:
I think travelling by plane can be difficult.

For example, sometimes the plane is delayed, and this is annoying.

Also, the airport is often very crowded, and it can be hard to find your way.

In my opinion, another problem is the food on the plane, because it is usually not very good.
questions.sampleB2: Well, flying can be a real hassle at times. To be honest, the biggest headache is probably delays — one hiccup and your whole itinerary falls apart. On top of that, you've got the endless security queues and the worry that your luggage might go missing. And let's face it, being cramped in a tiny seat for hours on end is far from comfortable.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men aeroportga boraman.

U yer gavjum va men kutaman.

Samolyot kechikadi va men xafa bo'laman.

Sumkam og'ir va menga yoqmaydi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, samolyotda sayohat qilish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin.

Masalan, ba'zida samolyot kechikadi va bu asabiylashtiradi.

Shuningdek, aeroport ko'pincha juda gavjum bo'ladi va yo'lingizni topish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Samolyotda sayohat qilish qulay bo'lsa-da, bir qator qiyinchiliklarni keltirib chiqaradi.

Eng ko'p uchraydigan muammolardan biri bu reyslarning kechikishi bo'lib, bu sayohat rejalarini buzishi va stressga olib kelishi mumkin, ayniqsa ulanadigan reyslar bilan.

Yana bir qiyinchilik - bu aeroportning o'zi, uzoq xavfsizlik tekshiruvi va oldindan kelish zarurati bilan.

Bundan tashqari, ko'plab reyslardagi cheklangan joy va noqulaylik uzoq safarlarni juda yoqimsiz qilishi mumkin.

Va nihoyat, har doim yo'qolgan yoki shikastlangan yuklar haqida xavotir bor, bu haqiqiy noqulaylik tug'dirishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are some challenges people face while traveling by plane?
sentenceStarters: "One of the main challenges is..." - "Asosiy qiyinchiliklardan biri..."
"Many travelers find it frustrating when..." - "Ko'p sayohatchilar ... bo'lganda xafa bo'lishadi..."
"From my experience, the biggest issue is..." - "Mening tajribamdan, eng katta muammo..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Traveling by plane, while convenient, comes with several notable challenges that passengers often face.
Firstly, there's the issue of flight delays and cancellations. Weather conditions, technical problems, or air traffic can cause significant disruptions to travel plans. This can be particularly stressful when passengers have connecting flights or important appointments.
Secondly, the airport experience itself can be challenging. Long security queues, strict baggage restrictions, and the need to arrive hours before departure can be time-consuming and exhausting. Many travelers find the check-in process and security screenings quite stressful.
Additionally, there are physical discomforts associated with flying. Jet lag can affect travelers crossing multiple time zones, leaving them tired and disoriented. The cramped seating on many flights, especially in economy class, can cause discomfort during long journeys.
Finally, there's the ever-present concern about lost luggage. Airlines occasionally mishandle baggage, leaving passengers without their belongings at their destination. Despite these challenges, air travel remains the fastest way to cover long distances.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Samolyotda sayohat qilish qulay bo'lsa-da, yo'lovchilar ko'pincha duch keladigan bir qator sezilarli qiyinchiliklar mavjud.

Birinchidan, reyslarning kechikishi va bekor qilinishi muammosi bor. Ob-havo sharoiti, texnik nosozliklar yoki havo harakati sayohat rejalariga sezilarli darajada ta'sir qilishi mumkin. Bu, ayniqsa, yo'lovchilarning ulanadigan reyslari yoki muhim uchrashuvlari bo'lsa, stressli bo'lishi mumkin.

Ikkinchidan, aeroportning o'zi ham qiyinchilik tug'dirishi mumkin. Uzoq xavfsizlik navbatlari, qat'iy bagaj cheklovlari va jo'nashdan bir necha soat oldin kelish zarurati vaqtni oladi va charchatadi. Ko'pgina sayohatchilar ro'yxatdan o'tish jarayoni va xavfsizlik tekshiruvlarini juda stressli deb bilishadi.

Bundan tashqari, uchish bilan bog'liq jismoniy noqulayliklar ham mavjud. Jet lag bir nechta vaqt zonalarini kesib o'tuvchi sayohatchilarga ta'sir qilishi, ularni charchagan va yo'nalishni yo'qotgan holda qoldirishi mumkin. Ko'pgina reyslardagi tor o'rindiqlar, ayniqsa ekonom-klassda, uzoq safarlar davomida noqulaylik tug'dirishi mumkin.

Va nihoyat, doimo yo'qolgan yuk haqida xavotir bor. Aviakompaniyalar ba'zan yuklarni noto'g'ri ishlaydi va yo'lovchilarni manzilga yetganda o'z narsalarisiz qoldiradi. Ushbu qiyinchiliklarga qaramay, havo transporti uzoq masofalarni bosib o'tishning eng tezkor usuli bo'lib qolmoqda.

questions.sampleA2: Travel is good. I like to go to new places and see new things. I can eat different food. But travel is sometimes expensive. I like travel with my family.
questions.sampleB1: I think traveling is really good for people. For example, you can learn about different cultures and see new places. It's also a good way to relax and forget about your problems for a while. However, it can be expensive, so you need to save money. In my opinion, everyone should travel if they have the chance.

For starters, it broadens your horizons — you get to rub shoulders with people from all walks of life and see how differently they live. It's also a brilliant way to switch off and leave your everyday worries behind. All in all, I reckon a good trip leaves you refreshed and far more open-minded.

Masalan, siz turli madaniyatlar haqida bilib olishingiz va yangi joylarni ko'rishingiz mumkin. Bu, shuningdek, dam olish va bir muddat muammolaringizni unutishning yaxshi usuli.

Sayohat qilganingizda, siz doimo notanish vaziyatlar va madaniyatlarga duch kelasiz, bu sizni moslashishga va o'rganishga majbur qiladi. Turli nuqtai nazarlarga duch kelish dunyo haqidagi tushunchangizni kengaytirishi va oldindan shakllangan tushunchalaringizga qarshi chiqishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, sayohat ko'pincha kundalik hayotning stresslaridan xalos bo'lishga imkon beradi, bu dam olish va ruhiy tetiklikni ta'minlaydi. Shuningdek, u sizga unutilmas xotiralar yaratish va turli xil kelib chiqishi bo'lgan odamlar bilan yangi munosabatlar o'rnatish imkoniyatini beradi. Umuman olganda, sayohatning foydalari shunchaki yangi joylarni ko'rishdan ancha uzoqroqqa boradi.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - How does traveling benefit people?
idioms: travel is fatal to prejudice - "sayohat xurofotga qarshi"
"A change is as good as a rest" - "O'zgarish dam olish kabi yaxshi"
sentenceStarters: "From my perspective, the greatest benefit of travel is..." - "Mening nuqtai nazarimdan, sayohatning eng katta foydasi..."
"I firmly believe that traveling helps people..." - "Men qat'iy ishonamanki, sayohat odamlarga ...da yordam beradi..."
"There's no denying that travel enriches..." - "Sayohat ...ni boyitishiga shubha yo'q..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Traveling offers numerous benefits that can positively impact people's lives in various ways.
Firstly, and perhaps most importantly, travel broadens the mind. When we visit new places, we're exposed to different cultures, traditions, and perspectives. This helps us become more open-minded and understanding of others. As Mark Twain said, "Travel is fatal to prejudice."
Secondly, traveling provides an excellent opportunity for personal growth. Navigating unfamiliar environments, solving unexpected problems, and communicating across language barriers all build confidence and problem-solving skills.
Additionally, travel is a powerful stress reliever. Taking a break from daily routines and work responsibilities allows people to recharge mentally. The excitement of exploring new places creates lasting memories and brings joy.
Furthermore, travel strengthens relationships. Whether traveling with family, friends, or a partner, shared experiences create stronger bonds. Even solo travel can lead to meeting new people and forming meaningful connections. Ultimately, travel enriches our lives in countless ways.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Sayohat odamlarning hayotiga turli yo'llar bilan ijobiy ta'sir ko'rsatadigan ko'plab foydalarni taklif etadi.

Birinchidan, va ehtimol eng muhimi, sayohat tafakkurni kengaytiradi. Biz yangi joylarga tashrif buyurganimizda, turli madaniyatlar, urf-odatlar va nuqtai nazarlar bilan tanishamiz. Bu bizga boshqalarga nisbatan bag'rikengroq va tushunuvchan bo'lishimizga yordam beradi. Mark Tven aytganidek, "Sayohat - xurofot uchun o'limdir."

Ikkinchidan, sayohat shaxsiy o'sish uchun ajoyib imkoniyat yaratadi. Notanish muhitda harakatlanish, kutilmagan muammolarni hal qilish va til to'siqlari orqali muloqot qilish ishonchni va muammolarni hal qilish qobiliyatini oshiradi.

Bundan tashqari, sayohat kuchli stressni kamaytiruvchi vositadir. Kundalik tartib va ish majburiyatlaridan tanaffus qilish odamlarga ruhiy jihatdan qayta tiklanishga imkon beradi. Yangi joylarni o'rganish hayajoni unutilmas xotiralar yaratadi va quvonch keltiradi.

Bundan tashqari, sayohat munosabatlarni mustahkamlaydi. Oila, do'stlar yoki sherik bilan sayohat qilishdan qat'i nazar, umumiy tajribalar kuchliroq aloqalarni yaratadi. Hatto yolg'iz sayohat ham yangi odamlar bilan uchrashishga va mazmunli aloqalar o'rnatishga olib kelishi mumkin. Oxir oqibat, sayohat hayotimizni son-sanoqsiz yo'llar bilan boyitadi.

questions.prompt: Describe the time when you shared a secret with another person.
questions.sampleA1: I have a secret. I tell my mom. She is nice. She don't tell.
questions.sampleA2: I told my sister a secret. It was about my birthday present. She was happy, and she didn't tell anyone. It was a good secret.
questions.sampleB1: I remember one time I shared a secret with my brother. It was about a surprise party for my dad. I told him because I needed his help to plan it. He promised not to tell, and he didn't. I think it's important to only share secrets with people you really trust.
questions.sampleB2: So, the time that springs to mind is when I confided in my best friend about the fact that I was planning to drop out of my university course. To be honest, it was eating me up inside, because I hadn't breathed a word of it to my family — I knew they'd hit the roof. One evening we were just chilling at her place, and it all came pouring out. She sat there, heard me out without judging me, and gave me some really level-headed advice. As for why I trusted her with something so personal, well, the thing is, she'd proven herself time and time again over the years. She'd never once let the cat out of the bag when I'd told her things in confidence, and I'd watched how discreetly she handled other people's business. On top of that, our friendship was built on mutual respect, so it felt like a safe bet. Now, can people who trust others too much end up getting hurt? Absolutely, I'd say they can. If you wear your heart on your sleeve and take everyone at face value, you're bound to get burned sooner or later, because let's face it, not everyone has your best interests at heart. That said, I don't think the answer is to shut people out completely. At the end of the day, you just have to strike a balance — give people the benefit of the doubt, but let them earn your trust bit by bit rather than handing it over blindly.
questions.uzSampleA1: Mening sirim bor. Men onamga aytaman. U yaxshi. U aytmaydi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men singlimga bir sir aytdim. Bu mening tug'ilgan kunim sovg'asi haqida edi. U xursand bo'ldi va hech kimga aytmadi. Bu yaxshi sir edi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Esimda, bir marta akam bilan bir sirni bo'lishgan edim. Bu dadam uchun kutilmagan tug'ilgan kun kechasi haqida edi. Men unga aytdim, chunki uni rejalashtirishda yordamiga muhtoj edim. U aytmaslikka va'da berdi va aytmadi. Menimcha, sirlarni faqat haqiqatan ham ishonadigan odamlaringiz bilan bo'lishish muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Bir marta men hamkasbimga kompaniyani tark etish rejalari haqida sirimni aytgan edim. Men hali menejerimga aytmagan edim va uning munosabati haqida xavotirda edim. Men bu hamkasbimga aytishni tanladim, chunki biz yaqin edik va ularning nuqtai nazarini qadrlardim. Ular hukm qilmasdan tinglashdi va foydali maslahatlar berishdi. Bu menga ishda ishonishingiz mumkin bo'lgan odamning bo'lishi muhimligini anglatdi, hatto bu faqat bir kishi bo'lsa ham. Albatta, bunday nozik ma'lumotlarni kimga ishonishingizga ehtiyot bo'lishingiz kerak, chunki hamma ham sir saqlay olmaydi.

bulletPoints: Describe the time when you shared a secret with another person.
Why did you think this person was reliable enough to tell your secret?
Can people who trust others too much get hurt?
questions.sampleAnswer:
I remember sharing a deeply personal secret with my closest friend about my struggles with anxiety during exam periods. It was something I hadn't told anyone else, not even my family.
I chose to confide in this particular friend because they had consistently demonstrated trustworthiness over the years. They had never broken my confidence before, and I had seen how they respectfully handled other people's personal information. Additionally, they were a good listener who offered support without judgment. Our friendship was built on mutual respect and understanding.
As for whether people who trust too much can get hurt – absolutely, they can. While trust is essential for meaningful relationships, blind trust can lead to disappointment and betrayal. Not everyone has good intentions, and some people may exploit others' openness for their own benefit.
However, I believe the solution isn't to become completely distrustful. Instead, we should practice cautious trust – giving people opportunities to prove themselves while being aware that trust should be earned gradually. As the proverb says, "Trust, but verify." Finding the right balance is key to protecting ourselves while still forming genuine connections.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Esimda, imtihon paytida meni bezovtalik qiynayotgani haqidagi juda shaxsiy sirimni eng yaqin do'stim bilan bo'lishganman. Bu haqda hech kimga, hatto oilamga ham aytmagan edim.

Men aynan shu do'stimga ishonishga qaror qildim, chunki u yillar davomida doimiy ravishda ishonchlilikni namoyon etgan edi. U avval hech qachon mening sirimni oshkor qilmagan va men uning boshqa odamlarning shaxsiy ma'lumotlariga qanday hurmat bilan munosabatda bo'lishini ko'rganman. Bundan tashqari, u yaxshi tinglovchi edi va hukm qilmasdan yordam taklif qilardi. Bizning do'stligimiz o'zaro hurmat va tushunishga asoslangan edi.

Haddan tashqari ishonadigan odamlar zarar ko'rishi mumkinmi degan savolga kelsak – albatta, ular zarar ko'rishi mumkin. Ishonch mazmunli munosabatlar uchun zarur bo'lsa-da, ko'r-ko'rona ishonch umidsizlik va xiyonatga olib kelishi mumkin. Hamma ham yaxshi niyatli emas va ba'zi odamlar boshqalarning ochiqligidan o'z manfaatlari yo'lida foydalanishi mumkin.

Biroq, menimcha, yechim butunlay ishonchsiz bo'lib qolish emas. Aksincha, biz ehtiyotkorlik bilan ishonchni amalda qo'llashimiz kerak – odamlarga o'zlarini isbotlash uchun imkoniyatlar berishimiz, shu bilan birga ishonch asta-sekin qozonilishi kerakligini anglashimiz kerak. Maqolda aytilganidek, "Ishon, lekin tekshir". O'zimizni himoya qilish va shu bilan birga chinakam aloqalarni o'rnatish uchun to'g'ri muvozanatni topish muhim.

questions.sampleA1: Zoo? Animals. I like animals. No ban.
questions.sampleA2: Zoos have animals. I like to see animals, and my children too. But the animals are sad, I think. Maybe zoos are bad, because animals are not happy there.
questions.sampleB1: I think zoos are difficult. On one hand, it's good to see the animals, especially for children, and maybe they learn something. But on the other hand, the animals are in cages, and that's not very nice for them. It's important to protect animals, but I'm not sure if zoos are the best way to do that. Maybe some zoos are okay, but others are not.
questions.sampleB2: This is a real hot-button issue, and to be honest, I can see valid arguments on both sides of the fence. On the one hand, those who want zoos banned do have a point. Cramming wild animals into tiny enclosures strikes many people as downright cruel, since the creatures are cut off from their natural habitat and can't really roam free the way they were meant to. Critics also argue that keeping animals purely for our entertainment is morally questionable, and there's no denying that some poorly run zoos treat their animals appallingly. On the other hand, I think banning zoos across the board would be throwing the baby out with the bathwater. A lot of modern, well-managed zoos play a crucial role in conservation — they run breeding programmes that have brought endangered species back from the brink of extinction. What's more, they give ordinary people, especially kids, the chance to get up close to wildlife they'd otherwise never lay eyes on, which can spark a lifelong passion for protecting nature. So where do I stand? Personally, I'm sitting on the fence a bit, but if push came to shove, I'd say an outright worldwide ban goes too far. Rather than shutting them all down, I reckon we should crack down hard on the ones that fall short and hold every zoo to much higher welfare standards. At the end of the day, a well-run zoo can genuinely do more good than harm — it's the bad ones we need to weed out.
questions.uzSampleA1: Hayvonot bog'i? Hayvonlar. Menga hayvonlar yoqadi. Taqiqlash yo'q.
questions.uzSampleA2: Hayvonot bog'larida hayvonlar bor. Men hayvonlarni ko'rishni yaxshi ko'raman, bolalarim ham. Lekin hayvonlar xafa, deb o'ylayman. Balki hayvonot bog'lari yomon bo'lishi mumkin, chunki hayvonlar u yerda baxtli emas.
questions.uzSampleB1: Menimcha, hayvonot bog'lari qiyin masala. Bir tomondan, hayvonlarni ko'rish yaxshi, ayniqsa bolalar uchun, va balki ular nimadir o'rganishar. Lekin boshqa tomondan, hayvonlar qafaslarda, va bu ular uchun unchalik yaxshi emas. Hayvonlarni himoya qilish muhim, lekin hayvonot bog'lari buni amalga oshirishning eng yaxshi usulimi, bilmayman. Balki ba'zi hayvonot bog'lari yaxshidir, lekin boshqalari emas.
questions.uzSampleB2: Hayvonot bog'lari taqiqlanishi kerakmi yoki yo'qmi, bu murakkab masala. Ular ta'lim olish imkoniyatlarini taqdim etsa va tabiatni muhofaza qilishga hissa qo'shsa-da, hayvonlarni asirlikda saqlashning axloqiy oqibatlari muhim ahamiyatga ega. Hayvonot bog'larini taqiqlash bo'yicha bahs ko'pincha hayvonlarning farovonligiga qaratilgan bo'lib, hayvonot bog'i muhitining tabiiy yashash joylarini takrorlash va ayrim turlarning xulq-atvor ehtiyojlarini qondirishdagi cheklanishlarini ta'kidlaydi. Biroq, ba'zilarning ta'kidlashicha, yaxshi boshqariladigan hayvonot bog'lari yo'qolib ketish xavfi ostida turgan turlarni saqlash va tabiatni muhofaza qilish to'g'risida jamoatchilik xabardorligini oshirishda muhim rol o'ynaydi. To'liq taqiq juda ekstremal bo'lishi mumkin, ammo qat'iyroq qoidalar va hayvonlarning farovonligiga katta e'tibor berish, albatta, zarur.

questions.sampleAnswer:
The debate about whether zoos should be banned worldwide raises important questions about animal welfare, conservation, and education. Let me examine both perspectives.
Those who support banning zoos make several compelling arguments. Firstly, animals in zoos often suffer from living in confined spaces that cannot replicate their natural habitats. Large animals like elephants and big cats, which naturally roam vast territories, can develop psychological problems and exhibit abnormal behaviors in captivity. Furthermore, the argument goes that wildlife has an inherent right to live freely in nature. Additionally, critics argue that zoos essentially exploit animals for human entertainment and profit, prioritizing visitor numbers over animal well-being.
On the other hand, there are strong arguments against a complete ban. Modern zoos play a crucial role in conservation efforts, particularly for endangered species. Breeding programs have helped save species from extinction. Zoos also provide invaluable educational opportunities, allowing people, especially children, to learn about wildlife and develop environmental awareness. Moreover, for some endangered animals, zoos provide safe havens from poaching and habitat destruction.
In my view, rather than banning zoos entirely, we should focus on improving standards and ensuring that animal welfare is the top priority. Well-managed sanctuaries that prioritize conservation over entertainment can be genuinely beneficial.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Hayvonot bog'larini butun dunyo bo'ylab taqiqlash kerakmi degan bahs hayvonlarning farovonligi, tabiatni muhofaza qilish va ta'lim haqida muhim savollarni o'rtaga tashlaydi. Keling, har ikki nuqtai nazarni ko'rib chiqaylik.

Hayvonot bog'larini taqiqlashni qo'llab-quvvatlovchilar bir nechta ishonarli dalillarni keltiradilar. Birinchidan, hayvonot bog'laridagi hayvonlar ko'pincha o'zlarining tabiiy yashash joylarini takrorlay olmaydigan cheklangan joylarda yashashdan aziyat chekadilar. Tabiatan keng hududlarda kezib yuradigan fillar va yirik mushuklar kabi katta hayvonlarda ruhiy muammolar paydo bo'lishi va asirlikda g'ayrioddiy xatti-harakatlar namoyon bo'lishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, yovvoyi tabiatning tabiatda erkin yashashga haqqi bor degan argument mavjud. Qo'shimcha ravishda, tanqidchilarning ta'kidlashicha, hayvonot bog'lari, asosan, hayvonlarni insonlar ko'ngilxushligi va foyda olish uchun ekspluatatsiya qiladi, tashrif buyuruvchilar sonini hayvonlarning farovonligidan ustun qo'yadi.

Boshqa tomondan, to'liq taqiqqa qarshi kuchli dalillar mavjud. Zamonaviy hayvonot bog'lari, ayniqsa yo'qolib ketish xavfi ostida turgan turlarni saqlashda muhim rol o'ynaydi. Ko'paytirish dasturlari turlarni yo'q bo'lib ketishdan saqlab qolishga yordam berdi. Hayvonot bog'lari, shuningdek, odamlarga, ayniqsa bolalarga yovvoyi tabiat haqida bilish va ekologik ongni rivojlantirish uchun bebaho ta'lim imkoniyatlarini beradi. Bundan tashqari, ba'zi yo'qolib ketish xavfi ostida turgan hayvonlar uchun hayvonot bog'lari brakonerlik va yashash joylarining yo'q qilinishidan xavfsiz boshpana beradi.

Mening fikrimcha, hayvonot bog'larini butunlay taqiqlash o'rniga, biz standartlarni yaxshilashga va hayvonlarning farovonligi ustuvor vazifa bo'lishini ta'minlashga e'tibor qaratishimiz kerak. Ko'ngilochar o'yin-kulgidan ko'ra tabiatni muhofaza qilishga e'tibor qaratadigan yaxshi boshqariladigan qo'riqxonalar haqiqatan ham foydali bo'lishi mumkin.
